lines.trans: It looks as though they are hosting a party tonight.
You did confirm our appointment, right?
Of course I did. Please wait just a little longer.
Never mind him, just leave him waiting out there.
I didn't come here to sip tea, I came here to do business.
Making guests wait while you play games takes some nerve.
I am planning to enter satellite broadcasting too.
I am the most famous adult video director in Japan.
Please grant me the broadcast rights to one satellite channel.
All of our satellite lines are already full.
Hear a man out to the end! My company brings in five billion yen a year!
Our vitality is on another level from pampered heirs talking pretty!

meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.

examples.text: バッチリです！商談するアポが取れましたよ。
examples.trans: Spot on! I secured an appointment for a business talk with the president.

examples.text: アポは取れてるんですよね？
examples.trans: You did confirm our appointment, right?

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Confident everyday word that works either before a predicate or as a standalone answer.

examples.text: もちろん手伝いますよ。

meanings.note: In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.
Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Signals recognizing someone ('Oh, Toshi!') or letting out a feeling ('Man, I'm hungry').
Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

そんな.gloss: such; that kind of; that much

meanings.note: Before たくさん, means 'that huge an amount'.

examples.text: そんな話は知りません。
examples.trans: I do not know such a story.

examples.text: そんな高いものは買えません。
examples.trans: I cannot buy something that expensive.

meanings.note: て-form 待って + ください is 'please wait'; causative お待たせして means 'having kept you waiting'.

おく.gloss: do in advance; keep in state

meanings.note: After a te-form (積んでおきました, contracted 入っとけ), indicates doing something in advance or staying put.

examples.text: 窓を開けておきました。
ここに置いておきます。
examples.trans: I will leave it here for now.

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.

examples.text: 俺は紅茶を飲みに来たんじゃない、ビジネスをしに来たんだ。
examples.trans: I didn't come here to sip tea, I came here to do business.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Irregular verb: くる -> きます -> きました.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Read ひと when standing as an independent noun.

examples.text: 親切な人に会いました。

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'game'.

examples.text: 新しいゲームを買った。

meanings.note: Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

examples.text: 近い将来爆発的に普及する衛星放送についてご存じですか？
examples.trans: Have you heard of satellite broadcasting, which will soon spread explosively?

examples.text: 衛星放送っていうのはどういうもんなんですか？
examples.trans: Just what kind of thing is satellite broadcasting?

examples.text: 衛星放送のチャンネルを一つ持てば、何でも好きに放送できるんです。
examples.trans: If you hold just one satellite channel, you can broadcast whatever you please.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.text: もう少しよく考えてみます。
examples.trans: I'll think about it a little more carefully.

meanings.note: Read にほん (Nihon) or にっぽん (Nippon).

examples.text: 日本の文化が好きです。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

examples.text: わたくしは日本で最も有名なアダルトビデオの監督です。
examples.trans: I am the most famous adult video director in Japan.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

examples.text: 衛星チャンネルの放送権を一つわたくしに許可してください。
examples.trans: Please grant me the broadcast rights to one satellite channel.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 衛星チャンネルの放送権を一つわたくしに許可してください。
examples.trans: Please grant me the broadcast rights to one satellite channel.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Native Japanese counter for general objects and abstract things like reasons.

examples.text: 理由がもう一つあります。
りんごを一つください。

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

examples.trans: All of our satellite lines are already full.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Covers everything from a casual chat to a business deal or idea.

examples.trans: Let us have a little talk.

meanings.en: nothing more than (after past verb); up to
meanings.note: After a plain verb + です (出店したまでです), modestly states 'we simply did that and nothing more'.

examples.text: 念のため聞いたまでです。
examples.trans: I merely asked just in case.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a business company or one's workplace.

examples.text: 新しい会社に入りました。

examples.trans: The company is near the station.

examples.text: 人の話は最後まで聞け！うちの会社の年商は五十億あるんだよ！
examples.trans: Hear a man out to the end! My company brings in five billion yen a year!

examples.text: ちなみに少なくとも年商は三千億だよね？
examples.trans: After all, each of us makes at least three hundred billion a year, right?

examples.text: 人の話は最後まで聞け！うちの会社の年商は五十億あるんだよ！
examples.trans: Hear a man out to the end! My company brings in five billion yen a year!

examples.text: だから五十億って威勢よく言われても笑っちゃうんだよな。
examples.trans: So when you brag about five billion yen, it just makes us laugh.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。
俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

examples.text: おもしれえじゃねえか、お宅の監督。
examples.trans: Your director is hilarious, isn't he!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Alone as 違う！ or 違います, means 'No, that's wrong!'.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。
